questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility to learn French and study at Sorbonne

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It's not easy to find information about the courses at Sorbonne. I only received a link to look at it a few weeks before the classes started (mid September for M1 and end September for M2)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of information at the university welcome day for exchange students/international students. This was super helpful and also where I met my friends

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied to the Cité Internationale and I got housing through this. It was easy to get and an amazing place to live

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Apply to the Cité Internationale!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Manual course registration so it had to be done by sending an e-mail to a guy who was really stressed and got angry at me a few times. I registered late for a course and they don't give you a confirmation of whether registration is confirmed so when I didn't hear anything, I assumed it was fine. When I showed up at the exam, my name wasn't there. Luckily they let me take the exam and get the credits, but not without being e-mail yelled at a bit...

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: No help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As explained, not very successful at first, but in the end everything worked out

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Stay patient. If you are not automatically added to the moodle of the course, make sure that you are registered

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There is very big difference between M1 and M2 courses. For M2 courses they expect you to be very independent and M1 courses are a lot easier. So if you want an easier exchange, I recommend taking mostly M1 courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not harder academically, but a lot more work and assignments than I'm used, and how they grade is not obvious at all, so it was very stressful

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
DALAS: Data science, Learning and Applications
BIMA: Fundamentals of image processing
RDFIA: Pattern recognition and machine learning for image
understanding
VISION: Advanced Methods for Computer Vision
BIOMED: Biomedical Imaging

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
IG3D: Introduction to Computer Graphics
pBIM: Projets BIM
PIMA: Projets IMA

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I definitely recommend taking project courses where you get weekly supervision to work on a project of a topic chosen from a list
Also the best course if you are interested in Machine learning on images was RDFIA. Very up-to-date, starting from the basics and reaching very advanced topics towards the semester. It's a hard course that requires you to work a lot during the semester (they have random tests), but it's very interesting and well organized
I cannot recommend BIMA and BIOMED as they are very outdated. It's good if you want a fundamental understanding of image processing, but espeically for BIMA, the exam is super hard and requires you to have very strong mathematical analysis skills

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I only know of the sports offers, but didn't use them. You have to be very fast at signing up for them (information given at welcome day)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Doing sports at the cité universitaire! They have a broad offer and it's a nice way to meet new people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Fontainebleau! Beautiful forest and the train is super cheap

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not too easy. I didn't make many French friends, mostly just internationals (which was also amazing)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I was very surprised by how many young French people I met that were not comfortable speaking French

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Bakeries, going out for drinks, a lot of cultural offers in the city that young people use a lot, such as going to indie movie theatres!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) I really recommend living at the Cité Internationale, it's such a special place
2) Use the museums in Paris! There are so many amazing ones and they are cheap or free if you are under 26
3) Try to take less credits as the course work can be very intense

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I really would not recommend French classes with Louis-Cesar, he's a bully. Otherwise I had good experience with taking French classes at Sorbonne

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends with people from all around the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academic load

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
